<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via IDataDriver (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d83052d5a4d0bd788e9460bbc1685553c49a0439` — the merge of head `aea485202eb2e4a293afa06bfc04cd8f2571bbcf` into base `895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d83052d5a4d0bd788e9460bbc1685553c49a0439 && git checkout d83052d5a4d0bd788e9460bbc1685553c49a0439
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 aea485202eb2e4a293afa06bfc04cd8f2571bbcf && git checkout -B drift-repro 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 && git merge --no-ff aea485202eb2e4a293afa06bfc04cd8f2571bbcf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1e2fb8541bc8c9fee8acfa4fa90fde98a92a22b4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/driver.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts, packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts

First review of this head. Claim: comment 6894293725. Tier evidence: `scripts/pm/verify-review-tier.mjs` on this review run's own transcript (`subagents/agent-a930767d0e984b1ae.jsonl` of the seat session) answers PASS, every turn served at the tier. Independence: the diff was claimed and dispatched by `domain:spec#4` (os-project-manager, claim 6892526787) and written by its card thread; os-elon-musk neither implemented nor dispatched it. For the record: card #33698 itself was filed by another os-elon-musk session (`domain:server#5`) as an epic child; filing is not dispatch, and the lane, claim, decisions and diff are all os-project-manager's.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds. `DriverCapabilitiesSchema` gains one optional boolean; every value accepted before is accepted now, absence parses as before, a non-boolean is refused (pinned in `driver.test.ts`). `authorable-surface/data.json` carries the new row; `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset` and the lint gate families are green on this head.
- The bit has its reader in the same change (`engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`, `supports.aggregationFilter === true` ANDed with method presence), so it is a live bit, not a declared-and-unread one. Memory, mongodb and odata declare nothing and keep the rows path; `TursoDriver` turns the bit off in remote mode, where the transport refuses the key.
- Point 1 (the in-memory null correction): the direction is right. It matches what `driver-sql`'s where compiler already answers and what the walker already answered for an absent column, and it is pinned on all three faces with an ablation. The reading "a patch-level correction, not a contract change" does not hold on the declaration axis, see S1.
- Point 2 (undeclared-column posture, seat decision 6893557132 option A): the seat's reading holds; this is not a `Clause-②` narrowing. The published position rule is that a per-aggregation filter answers what its `where` twin answers (#20148, #21255, #21299; rows 1 to 4 of `aggregation-filter-where-doors.test.ts` already refuse a key or a reference that names no field at that position, before any read). The one case that answered 200 was recorded in that file as a fail-open posture "so a change on either side is seen", not as an accepted shape: a `{ $field }` comparison across two column classes is refused whenever both sides are declared, and it slipped through only because one side had no declaration. No declared shape loses acceptance. The split that remains is between drivers, as it already is for the `where` position, and the changeset and the new no-bit case say so. The declarations need no change on this account.
- Point 3 (security parity) holds on this head, read at the rule level. The epic rule is that read scope and the tenant wall stay on the pushed-down statement: both arrive on the statement's own `where` exactly as they do for an unfiltered aggregate, the measure filter is compiled separately and can only narrow inside them, and a compile that cannot be isolated is refused rather than emitted. The field-readability refusal applies at the measure-filter position before any driver is reached, on both paths. `aggregate-measure-filter-pushdown.test.ts` pins it through the REST door with the real security layer and the `isolated` posture, asserting which driver method ran on each path; the driver test pins the wall with two organizations. I found no path in the diff where a measure filter widens the row set or where scope is dropped.
- Divergence 2 (ordering of non-temporal text under a non-C collation, ungated): acceptable as declared for the measured backends. `filter.zod.ts` already states that order is permitted and not promised, and after pushdown the measure filter agrees with the `where` of the same datasource. The unmeasured dialects are a different matter, see S2.

### ② Semver level

- `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` is right and stays right under S1: `added` and `semantic` both take at least `minor` on a moved package, and the level follows the kind alone. `patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/driver-turso` is right (same shape as #33518, record ID: 6885895029).
- The kind itself is wrong as declared, see S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No id materialisation and no in-app join is added where SQL can push down; the change removes a whole-set read.
- The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay write to note.
- CI on this head is not green: `Type Check · workspace` (and the `TypeScript Type Check` roll-up) is red on the diff's own lines, see M1. The Test Core, Test UI and build jobs were still running when this record was written.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`: an opt-in bit ANDed with method presence is the right shape. `aggregate()` predates the key, a subclass can inherit a compiler its transport refuses, and the engine fallback is always correct, so absence changing nothing is true. The promise text is where the two findings below sit. `packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts`: the `aggregate()` TSDoc now matches the engine's gate.

Implementing files: the engine gate is a strict `=== true` (a truthy non-boolean stays on the rows path, pinned). The driver compiles the predicate with the same where compiler and emits no `ELSE`, so `count` cannot count rejected rows; a group the filter empties folds to the existing empty-group values. The walker change is five operators wide, leaves the equality family, the listed no-value operators and a null comparand alone, and negation keeps the null row as the lowering's totality rule expects.

M1 (must-fix) — the head does not type-check. `Type Check · workspace` fails in `packages/drivers/driver-sql` with TS2769 at `src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts` 322, 324, 371 and 373: the four `this.knex.raw(..., filterBindings)` calls this PR adds pass `unknown[]` (from `readonly unknown[]` in `compileMeasureFilter`) where knex wants its raw-binding type. These are the diff's own lines, so the red is not a merge-base signature. The PR body's "124 run, 124 exit 0" did not include this check. Type the lifted bindings as knex's binding type at the point they are sliced, rather than casting at the four call sites.

S1 (should-fix) — `Metadata-protocol: added` under-declares; the line should read `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, in the PR body and in the changeset body. Seat decision 6892621130 reads the walker's null rule as a correction below the declaration axis. The test the fleet has already ruled is whether a stored declaration keeps validating and now selects other rows (#33518, record ID: 6885895029: "a stored filter keeps validating but now matches different rows; that is a changed meaning"). That is exactly what happens here, and on every driver: a stored `having` such as `avg_amount $lte 0` kept an empty group and no longer does (`having` is engine-evaluated on driver-sql too); a stored measure filter on a driver without the bit, and a plugin driver's `where`, stop counting rows with no value under `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte` and `$between`. #33518 was itself a correction of a silent wrong answer and was still ruled `semantic`. The spec sentence the decision leans on ("null is not ordered", `filter.zod.ts`) is written about a null comparand, not a null column, so the column-side rule is new published meaning rather than an existing promise being met. With `added` also present the precedence in AGENTS.md step 3 gives `semantic`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` stays. The level does not move. The changeset's "What answers differently in memory" paragraph already says the right thing in user words; only the kind line is wrong. A kind other than `none` also owes the PR body its `Skills-docs:` line, which is absent today.

S2 (should-fix) — the bit's TSDoc promises more than was measured, and `driver-sql` declares the bit on dialects nobody measured. The text names one latitude (ordering of non-temporal text) and then says every other operator answers alike. That was measured on SQLite and PostgreSQL 16 only. `driver-sql` also targets MySQL and SQL Server, declares `aggregationFilter: true` there unconditionally, and its where compiler emits a plain `=` and `in` for text equality, which those backends decide by the column collation; their default collations are case-insensitive, where the in-memory path compares exactly. So on those dialects a stored measure filter like `stage $eq 'won'` can start counting `Won` rows after this PR, silently, and the published promise says it cannot. I did not measure it either; the point is that the schema text asserts it. Either declare the bit only on the dialects that were measured, or widen the stated latitude to what is true: text comparison in a measure filter is the backend collation's, as for the `where` of the same datasource (ordering everywhere, equality and membership on a case- or accent-insensitive collation), with the unmeasured dialects named in the TSDoc as they are in the changeset.

Nits, no effect on the verdict:

- N1 (nit): `filter.zod.ts` should state the column-side rule (a column with no value fails an ordering operator) beside the comparand-side sentence, so the walker's docblock cites text that says it. Follow-up card.
- N2 (nit, prose face): the bench scenario note is now true only for drivers without the bit; the PR body already says so.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8e48947dc02f3a076122abda2c2d81be1ad1c3d0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/data-driver.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/data/driver.test.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json, packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts, packages/objectql/src/in-memory-aggregation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts

Read at 2026-11-15T13:43Z. Claim: comment 6894944006. Handed to review#2 by review#1 (6894936609 on mailbox #33873). Delta review of the earlier record, ID 6894395884, which reviewed head `1e2fb854` in full and raised M1, S1, S2, N1 and N2. Two commits sit on top of that head: `4775f3f4` (the binding types in `sql-driver-aggregation.ts`) and `8e48947d` (declarations and prose). `git diff 1e2fb854 8e48947d` touches eight files: the changeset, `query-syntax.mdx`, the three generated driver reference pages, `sql-driver-aggregation.ts`, `sql-driver.ts` and `driver.zod.ts`. Every other file of the PR is byte-identical to the head the earlier record judged, and the merge base is the same (`1e65a389`).

Closures, by id:

- M1: closed.
- S1: closed.
- S2: closed.

One new finding on this head, S3 below, on a `hits` file the delta did not touch.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta changes no accept set and no exported type. `DriverCapabilitiesSchema` is the same shape as on the earlier head: one optional boolean, absence parses as before, a non-boolean is refused. Only the bit's TSDoc and its `.describe()` string moved. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` still holds.
- The `.describe()` string is published text, and it was regenerated into the four rows of `content/docs/references/data/driver.mdx`, `driver-sql.mdx` and `driver-nosql.mdx`; the rows on the head match the schema string word for word. `authorable-surface/data.json` holds the key only, so it is unchanged and right. `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Spec property liveness` are green.
- `4775f3f4` changes types only: the return type of `compileMeasureFilter` reads `readonly Knex.Value[]` and `filterBindings` is `Knex.Value[]`. No emitted SQL, binding order or guard moves, so every judgment the earlier record made on the driver compile holds unchanged.
- The `query-syntax.mdx` row removal is a prose face and the lane seat's to accept; I note only that amendment 6894446721 names removal as one of its two allowed outcomes.
- The earlier record's other derived judgments (the live reader in the same change, the walker's null rule in direction, seat decision 6893557132 read as a refusal of a malformed filter and not a narrowing, security parity at the rule level, the text-ordering latitude) rest on files this delta does not touch, and I confirm them on this head. One extra attempt to break the design: a composed `ReadableIds` leaf compiles to a subquery, which SQL Server refuses inside an aggregate. It cannot reach a measure filter, because the engine refuses that leaf at every position but the statement's own `where` (`filter-comparand-shape.ts`), so the pushed-down `CASE WHEN` never holds a subquery.

### ② Semver level

- Check-runs on `8e48947d`, read at 2026-11-15T13:41Z: 71 runs. 56 success, 12 skipped, 1 cancelled, 2 still in progress (`Test Core (3/8)` and `Test Core (8/8)`). No failure. The cancelled run is a superseded `PR-body guards` run; its sibling on the same head is green.
- `Type Check · workspace` is green on this head (completed 13:41:00Z), and so are the `TypeScript Type Check` roll-up, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` and `Type Check UI`. On `1e2fb854` the same check was red. That is the evidence M1 closes on.
- `Check Changeset` is green (both runs). `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` with `patch` on objectql, driver-sql and driver-turso satisfies the level rule: a declared kind takes at least `minor` on one moved package. All four packages sit in the changeset `fixed` group, so they publish at one level in any case.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` is now the line in the changeset body and in the PR body, and the two agree. It is the right kind: a stored `having`, measure filter or plugin-driver `where` keeps validating and selects other rows under the null rule, and `semantic` takes precedence over `added` (AGENTS.md, landing step 3). The PR body carries `Skills-docs: follow-up #33868`; whether that card exists and says what is owed is the lane seat's checklist line, not read here.
- Clause-②: `yes (widening: one optional DriverCapabilities bit)`, identical in the PR body and the changeset, and right.
- The ADR-0087 question. No entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` is owed, and that is right for the walker's null rule. Read on the tree: `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` asks for a disposition only from a changeset that declares breaking, by one of five signals (`breakingDeclaration`: a `major` bump, a BREAKING banner, a `!` summary, the `(narrowing)` arm, or the `narrowed` kind). This changeset carries none of them. `semantic` adds no signal by ruling A, the gate's self-test pins that, and the 2026-11-12 addendum to ADR-0087 says `added`, `semantic` and `none` keep the exemption. AGENTS.md step 3 asks for the disposition from a breaking changeset only. On the merits the ledger feeds `objectstack migrate meta` and the upgrade guide with edits an author must make; the null rule refuses nothing and prescribes no rewrite, and its notice is the changeset paragraph "What answers differently in memory", which ships in the CHANGELOG. One correction of wording only: the PR body says the changeset "is exempt"; more exactly, the gate never judges it, since it is not a breaking declaration.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The last dev report on the card (6894248671) has `open_questions: []` and `security_findings: none`. The two earlier questions were answered by seat decisions 6892621130 (option C) and 6893557132 (option A), both judged in the earlier record. No report for round 2 is on the card, so round 2 raises no open question there.
- The round-2 plan (6894412038) is followed on each point: bindings typed where they are sliced with no cast at the call sites, the kind line changed, option (b) for the latitude, N1 filed as a follow-up.
- The PR body says the maintainer approved the out-of-surface test and comment edits by name in the dev's card thread. That approval is not on the card, so it is taken as stated and is the lane seat's to hold.
- No `hits` path is under `skills/**`, so the security-label rule does not apply.
- No in-app join or id materialisation is added; the earlier record's reading stands.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts` (changed in the delta). The rewritten latitude now says only what holds on every dialect `driver-sql` declares the bit on. Sentence by sentence: text comparison in a measure filter is the backend collation's, and the filter answers what its `where` twin answers. That is true by construction on every dialect, because the predicate comes from the same where compiler (`applyFilters`) and is placed in `CASE WHEN` unchanged. Ordering of non-temporal text is "not promised in any case", which is what `filter.zod.ts` says of the comparison operators. Equality and membership "follow the collation too", with the `stage $eq 'won'` example, stated as what a case- or accent-insensitive collation does and not as something measured. The measured list names SQLite, PostgreSQL 16 with `C.UTF-8` and PostgreSQL 16 with ICU `en-US`; MySQL and SQL Server are named as not measured, and the case-folding there is worded "expected", not asserted. The closing sentence is limited to "wherever measured". The first paragraph's promise (the in-memory answer) is now followed directly by the latitude it inherits, so the two no longer contradict. The `.describe()` string carries the same exception in one clause. S2 asked for exactly this, by its second option, and the seat chose that option on the card with a reason that holds: gating the bit by dialect would keep MySQL and SQL Server on a path that answers differently from their own `where`.

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts` (changed in the delta). The three new comment lines say the bit is declared on every dialect, that text comparison is then the collation's as for the datasource's `where`, and point at the bit's TSDoc for the measured dialects. Each is true against the code: `supports` is one literal for every dialect, and the compile uses `applyFilters`.

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-aggregation.ts` (changed in the delta). The bindings are typed at the point they are sliced from knex's own `toSQL()`, as the earlier record asked, with no cast at the four `knex.raw` calls. The type is honest: the values are what knex itself produced for the same builder. The check-run is the verdict, and it is green.
